seoTitle: How to Change Chart Layout on TradingView 2026
metaDescription: Learn how to switch between single, double, and quad chart layouts in TradingView, sync charts, and save your custom workspace.
intro: Tracking multiple assets, timeframes, or strategies at once is much easier with TradingView's multi-chart layouts than flipping between tabs. This guide covers adjusting your chart layout, switching between single and multi-chart views, and organizing your workspace for better analysis.

steps.heading: Open the layout options
steps.body: Use the layout icon on TradingView's top panel to see the available chart arrangement options.

steps.heading: Switch between single, double, and quad views
steps.body: Choose the number of charts you want visible at once, depending on how many symbols or timeframes you're tracking simultaneously.

steps.heading: Align layouts vertically or horizontally
steps.body: Adjust whether your multiple charts are arranged in rows or columns to best fit your monitor and workflow.

steps.heading: Sync charts together
steps.body: Enable chart syncing so scrolling or changing the symbol on one chart updates the others in the layout automatically.

steps.heading: Save your custom layout
steps.body: Once your workspace is set up the way you like, save it so you can return to the same multi-chart arrangement in future sessions.

faq.question: Is multi-chart layout free on TradingView?
faq.answer: Basic multi-chart layouts are available through TradingView's trial or paid plans, with the free plan generally limited to fewer simultaneous charts.

faq.question: Can I sync different symbols across multiple charts?
faq.answer: Yes, chart syncing lets you keep timeframes or crosshair movement aligned across multiple charts, even if each shows a different symbol.

faq.question: How many charts can I view at once?
faq.answer: TradingView supports layouts ranging from a single chart up to multiple charts arranged in a grid, depending on your plan.

faq.question: Can I save multiple layouts for different strategies?
faq.answer: Yes, TradingView lets you save several custom layouts so you can switch between different workspace setups depending on what you're analyzing.
